parsed.explanation: Combined federal-state regime creates tier-1 universal exposures: binary passport policy with discrepancy-based refusal and possible fraud ineligibility, federal and widespread state facility bans including a documented trespass arrest and men's-ward holding, and birth-sex custody/hormone-removal practices. Immigration-custody reports of forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse add severe custody risk. Courts have enjoined some orders, hate-crime law covers gender identity, and no execution or systematic imprisonment for presence is documented, keeping the case above severe-risk anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport sex-marker restrictions in effect after November 2025; entry cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Confiscation/blocking and detentions reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, limited waivers exist; litigation pending.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger refusal, investigation, detention and birth-sex placement, compounding facility and custody exposures.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections model includes hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. Bathroom trespass arrest led to 24 hours in men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires wilful entry plus refusal to depart; maximum example 60 days. No documented execution for trans presence.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest or immigration detention converts a document/facility encounter into birth-sex custody and care interruption.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal binary definition bars congruent government single-sex facilities; many states ban identity-congruent use in government buildings/schools, some private settings, and four make it criminal in circumstances. One handcuffed capitol-restroom arrest documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states plus capital district mapped as having no ban in listed categories, though other sex-definition laws may apply; statutory exemptions exist.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Everyday facility use, hospital or school access can lead to trespass exposure and police involvement.

care_services.exposure: Division SAFE Act, upheld January 2026, bans starting hormones/blockers and all transition surgery for minors, bars Medicaid payment any age, and threatens provider licence loss. Prison funding bar effective July 2026 has no taper.
care_services.protection: Minors already in treatment may continue under SAFE Act; some comparable measures elsewhere blocked by courts, showing contestation.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing medication continuity may face provider refusal or custody-related hormone removal despite continuation language.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders and counterterrorism language frame 'radical gender ideology' and 'radically pro-transgender' groups as threats; federal law enforcement directed to investigate schools facilitating social transition. Poll cited 66% support for assigned-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No documented reward criterion based on gender ideology; several orders blocked/enjoined; national employment and hate-crime protections remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises police discretion, outing and escalation risk beyond formal facility/document rules.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor cannot start hormones/blockers or have transition surgery in division; school sports restricted to assigned sex; guardian/provider face investigation, licence or prosecution risks for facilitating transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Existing treatment may continue; SAFE Act sunsets 2027 but permanence/ballot efforts documented, so protection is time-limited and contested.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling family seeking school, sports or care encounters state bans even if entry itself is allowed; custody or care interruption affects parent/guardian decisions.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated division-specific trans violence incident with outcome documented. Federal/state structures plus document enforcement create police-contact risk; national custody abuse reports show institutional hostility in some settings.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime statute explicitly covers gender identity; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity, though state coverage is uneven nationally.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Protection depends on reporting and police/court response; functioning institutions also efficiently enforce hostile facility/document policies.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport litigation unresolved; many orders in litigation; division care ban finally upheld by state highest court; no division-specific airport screening rule documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties lawsuits, injunctions/enjoinments of some orders, legal-aid FAQ, sanctuary ordinances in two cities, and hate-crime recourse documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow, uneven and cannot reliably prevent refusal, arrest, detention or care denial during a short visit.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar or slightly higher: both involve birth-sex custody placement with assault/harm and slow remedies. This case adds entry refusal/fraud risk and criminal facility exposure, but lacks documented routine prison assaults for visitors and has more functioning courts/injunctions, so a little above 0.25.

Lower: 0.35-B has hours-long stops, fines and no imprisonment. Here bathroom trespass can mean jail and men's-ward holding, entry can mean refusal/permanent-ineligibility consideration, and custody reports include forced labour and sexual abuse.

Materially lower: 0.55-C centres on ward placement and delayed nonurgent care with patient advocates. Here facility bans are criminalised in some states, federal document policy affects entry, and custody care is removed, with federal-state interactions escalating beyond service denial.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is document discrepancy or facility use leading to refusal, trespass arrest, detention, birth-sex placement and interrupted care. State care and surgical-document rules mainly affect residents, but the minor-care ban is traveler-facing if care is sought. Protections—valid existing X passports, exemptions, hate-crime coverage, injunctions and legal aid—are real yet do not reliably prevent the documented exposures during travel. No capital or systematic imprisonment pathway is documented, but severe custody and universal facility/document exposure place the regime between the 0.25 and 0.35 anchors.
